statement: A boolean-only abstention flag conflates a self-imposed, disclosed coverage limit (e.g. a size cap or extension exclusion the tool itself declared) with a genuine read failure (data the tool expected to read and could not) -- and a composite-score denominator that keeps every abstention at a punitive zero silently punishes the self-imposed case, which should instead be excluded from the average like any other measurement gap. Incident: cejel's scorer built its 'read-failure abstentions stay in the denominator at zero' set from a single insufficientData=true boolean with no reason, so a file skipped only because it exceeded the tool's own declared size limit was treated identically to a file the filesystem genuinely refused to read -- both zeroed a criterion into the composite instead of excluding it. Only a real read failure (evidence the tool believed existed and lost) should stay in a composite's denominator at zero; a self-imposed, disclosed limit should exclude the criterion from the average exactly like any other 'nothing to measure' gap. Fix: carry the actual reason on the abstention (a reason field/set, not a bare boolean) so the scorer can tell the two apart, defaulting an absent reason to the historically conservative choice (treat as a real failure) so no existing signal producer's behavior silently changes. Rule: when a boolean 'gap' flag can be caused by more than one underlying condition and those conditions deserve different downstream treatment, the flag needs a reason attached before the two conditions are accidentally scored the same way; do not discover this by noticing punitive scores after the fact.
